_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of organ rejection in adult patients receiving a kidney transplant, in combination with basiliximab induction, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids; for use only in EBV seropositive patients

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study IM103008 (Study 1), recipients of living and standard criteria deceased donor kidneys
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, partially-blinded, active-controlled: IV belatacept (MI and LI) or cyclosporine; basiliximab induction, MMF and corticosteroids
pivotal_trials.population: De novo adult kidney transplant recipients of living donor and standard criteria donor kidneys; enrolled 666 patients at 104 sites worldwide
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: composite of patient and graft survival at 12 months, a composite renal impairment endpoint (measured GFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 at Month 12 or decrease in measured GFR >=10 from Month 3 to Month 12), and incidence of acute rejection by 12 months; FDA based efficacy decision on biopsy confirmed acute rejection (non-inferiority)
pivotal_trials.n: Recommended (LI) regimen N=226 vs cyclosporine N=221
pivotal_trials.result: Efficacy Failure by Year 1: 49 (21.7%) belatacept vs 37 (16.7%) cyclosporine (difference 4.9; 97.3% CI -3.3, 13.2); non-inferiority margin met. Patient and graft survival at Year 3: 206 (91.2%) belatacept vs 192 (86.9%) cyclosporine (4.3; 97.3% CI -2.2, 10.8)

nct_ctgov.title: Belatacept Evaluation of Nephroprotection and Efficacy as First-line Immunosuppression (BENEFIT)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study IM103027 (Study 2), recipients of extended criteria donor kidneys
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, partially-blinded, active-controlled: IV belatacept (MI and LI) or cyclosporine; basiliximab induction, MMF and corticosteroids
pivotal_trials.population: De novo adult kidney transplant recipients of extended criteria donor kidneys; enrolled 543 patients at 79 sites worldwide
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary composite of patient and graft survival at 12 months and composite renal impairment endpoint; acute rejection by 12 months was a secondary endpoint in IM103027
pivotal_trials.n: Recommended (LI) regimen N=175 vs cyclosporine N=184
pivotal_trials.result: Efficacy Failure by Year 1: 51 (29.1%) belatacept vs 52 (28.3%) cyclosporine (0.9; 97.3% CI -9.7, 11.5). Patient and graft survival at Year 3: 143 (81.7%) belatacept vs 143 (77.7%) cyclosporine (4.0; 97.3% CI -5.4, 13.4)

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Belatacept in Subjects Who Are Undergoing a Renal Transplant

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) included urinary tract infection (37% vs 36% cyclosporine), diarrhea (39% vs 36%), constipation (33% vs 35%), anemia, pyrexia, and headache (21% vs 18%). Serious risks: increased risk of PTLD (predominantly CNS), other malignancies, serious infections, and PML. Serious infections occurred in 36% of belatacept patients vs 39% cyclosporine by Year 3
target_moa: A selective T-cell costimulation blocker that binds CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, blocking CD28-mediated costimulation of T lymphocytes and inhibiting T lymphocyte proliferation and cytokine production (IL-2, interferon-gamma, IL-4, TNF-alpha)
modality: Soluble fusion protein (modified extracellular domain of CTLA-4 fused to Fc of human IgG1) produced by recombinant DNA technology

boxed_warning.content: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, other malignancies, and serious infections: increased risk of PTLD predominantly involving the CNS (particularly in EBV-seronegative patients; use only in EBV seropositive patients); increased susceptibility to infection and malignancies from immunosuppression; use in liver transplant patients not recommended due to increased risk of graft loss and death; only physicians experienced in immunosuppressive therapy should prescribe

rems.type: REMS consisting of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and timetable for submission of assessments, to inform healthcare providers of the increased risk of PTLD (predominantly CNS) and PML and to inform patients of the serious risks associated with belatacept

advisory_committee.vote: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (March 2010) voted 13 'yes' and 5 'no' on whether the overall benefits outweigh the risks and the application should be approved

description.text: Updated labeling to incorporate long-term efficacy and safety data from Long-Term Extension of Phase 3 studies in kidney transplant recipients

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for update of the labeling to incorporate the long-term efficacy and safety data of the Long-Term Extension of Phase 3 studies IM103008 and IM103027 in kidney transplant recipients.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted February 28, 2008 for prophylaxis of organ rejection in renal allograft recipients

citations.quote: BMS requested orphan drug designation on November 19, 2006, and pursuant to section 526 of FD&C Act, belatacept was granted orphan status on February 28, 2008 for “prophylaxis of organ rejection in renal allograft recipients.” Therefore, the application is exempt from user fees and from PREA requirements.

summary.text: Belatacept (Nulojix), an orphan-designated selective T-cell costimulation blocker, was submitted June 30, 2009 (received July 1, 2009), presented to the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee, received a Complete Response letter on May 1, 2010 for manufacturing and clinical deficiencies, and was approved June 15, 2011 after submission of 3-year clinical data, with a REMS and postmarketing requirements/commitments

citations.quote: Conduct a prospective observational study utilizing data from the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) on the incidence rates of post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) in US adult kidney-only transplant recipients who are treated with belatacept compared to recipients treated with calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-based regimens.

requirement.text: Conduct a prospective registry of belatacept use in US adult kidney-only transplant recipients to determine incidence rates of PTLD, CNS PTLD, and PML in EBV seropositive recipients treated with belatacept in clinical practice (Protocol IM103076)
